text: Casual dress code: everyday comfort-first clothing. Jeans, chinos, T-shirts, casual knits, sneakers or clean flats are all acceptable. No formality expectations; prioritize the wearer's comfort and personal expression.

Smart casual: polished but relaxed. Combine a casual base with one elevated piece, e.g. dark jeans or chinos with a collared shirt, fine-gauge knit, or an unstructured blazer; loafers or clean minimal sneakers. Avoid athletic wear and distressed items.

Business casual: professional without a suit. Trousers or a knee-length skirt with a button-down, blouse, or knit; an optional blazer. Closed-toe leather shoes or loafers. No jeans, sneakers, or logos in conservative offices.

Semi-formal (incl. cocktail): a step below formal. A dark suit or a cocktail dress / dressy separates; refined fabrics, minimal patterning, leather dress shoes or heels. Appropriate for evening events, cocktail parties, and daytime weddings.

Formal: a dark, well-tailored suit or a floor-length or elegant evening dress. Muted, sophisticated palette; polished dress shoes or heels; understated accessories. Expected at evening weddings and upscale events without a black-tie call.
Black tie: a tuxedo (black dinner jacket, satin lapels, black bow tie) or a formal floor-length gown. Strictly evening. No business suits, no colored shirts; keep accessories minimal and classic.

Office / work eligibility: default to business casual unless the workplace is explicitly formal or creative-casual. Choose pieces that layer for indoor climate control and read as put-together for meetings.

Job interview eligibility: dress one notch above the company's daily norm; business casual to formal. Conservative colors, minimal distractions, well-fitted tailoring. Signals seriousness and respect.
Evening wedding eligibility: formal to black-tie depending on the invitation. Favor refined fabrics and a considered palette; avoid white/ivory (reserved for the couple) and overly casual pieces.
Daytime / outdoor wedding eligibility: semi-formal. Cocktail dress or dressy separates; lighter fabrics and colors suit daytime. Consider terrain (garden, beach) for footwear.
Dinner date eligibility: smart casual is the reliable default; nudge toward the venue's formality. One statement piece plus a clean, well-fitted base reads intentional without trying too hard.
Brunch / daytime social eligibility: smart casual with a relaxed, daytime palette. Comfortable but considered; breathable fabrics for seated outdoor settings.
Funeral / memorial eligibility: formal and subdued. Dark, muted colors (black, charcoal, navy); conservative coverage; no bright colors or flashy accessories, out of respect.
Beach / seaside eligibility: casual and heat-appropriate. Light, breathable fabrics, sun protection, and footwear that tolerates sand. Cover-ups elevate a swim base for nearby cafes.

Freezing weather (below 0C): base layer, insulating mid-layer, and a windproof/insulated outer coat; cover extremities with hat, gloves, scarf. Warmth outranks silhouette; choose the heaviest wardrobe items (warmth 4-5).
Cold weather (0-10C): a warm outer layer over a mid-layer (sweater or jacket). Long sleeves and full-length legwear; closed shoes. Favor wardrobe items rated warmth 3-4.
Cool weather (10-16C): a light jacket, cardigan, or blazer over a top; layering lets the wearer adapt. Warmth 2-3 items work well.
Mild weather (16-22C): a single comfortable layer with an optional light topper for evening. Most warmth 1-2 items are comfortable.
Warm weather (22-28C): breathable single layers, shorter sleeves or hems, natural fibers like linen and cotton. Choose the airiest wardrobe items (warmth 0-1).
Hot weather (above 28C): minimal, loose, light-colored breathable clothing; prioritize sun protection and airflow. Avoid heavy or dark heat-absorbing fabrics; warmth 0 items only.
